ergo.description: The version of the spec the report follows

engine.description: What made the report: ergo- and the engine, like ergo-rego or ergo-rust, and its version. A report's hash leaves it out.

compliant.description: true when there's at least one requirement and none is not_met

subjects.description: The subjects the requirements use, directly or through the subjects they narrow or read from, by name.

description.description: The subject's description, or "" when it has none.

from.description: How the subject is found, as a from line is written, or <invalid from> when it is written wrong.

identified_by.description: The path of the subject's id, or null when it has none and the whole subject is its id.

parts.description: Every part the subject has, including the ones it keeps from a subject it narrows, by alias.

from.description: The part's path, written as a sentence writes it, or <invalid from> when it is written wrong.

identified_by.description: The path of the part's id, <invalid identified_by> when it is written wrong, or null when it has none.

causes.description: The causes of the rows that would be violations of the requirement, worst first, each with how many rows have it. Empty when the requirement is met or not_applicable.

checks.description: Each check as written, plus the checks Ergo adds, which start with $.

require.description: The require the requirement was written with, or every by default.

subject.description: The name of the subject the requirement checks, or null when it names none or one that isn't in the policy's subjects. Ergo's own `$policy` requirement names `$policy`.

locations.description: Where the value was read, as JSON Pointers from the root of the input, or $params: and a pointer from the root of the params. Empty when no location could be given.

outcome.description: Only on failed rows, on an entry that reads a path: how the read ended, with usable for a value the check can use, and unusable for one that was read but the check can't use. A value Ergo works out, like a count of or a sum of, has none.

part.description: Present when the input was read through a part: the part's alias as the check writes it, and the id read inside the part, or null.

type.description: The name of the requirement's subject, the name of the ancestor whose ids a `$unique_ancestor_ids` row checks, or `$policy` for the row of Ergo's own `$policy` requirement.

id.description: The subject's id, null for the rows of the checks Ergo adds to a requirement, or `$policy` for the row of Ergo's own `$policy` requirement.

in.description: Only for a child subject, or for an ancestor that a `$unique_ancestor_ids` row checks and that is a child subject itself: the name and id of each subject it was read from, its parent and, three subjects deep, its grandparent.

message.description: Only on failed rows: what Ergo found, in plain words, like approver is "ana", and author is "ana".

failures.description: On every failed row of a check, an $applies row or a $min_subjects row, and never on a passed row: every part that failed, at every level, as the rule row.parts says, [] when no part has an entry.

name.description: The option's name, the sentence as written, the item like item 2 of xs, or the list as the message names it.

inputs.description: What this part read at its own level.

failures.description: The parts under this one that failed.

message.description: What the row's message says about this part, without the names in front, or empty.
